tested_scope: Three witness compositions across five rollback/stateless-reconstruction scenarios; finite logical matrix, not a production-rate estimate.
observation: A mutable named anchor plus immutable object identity blocks ref-only ABA only while the selector's expected immutable SHA survives outside the ref-recreation failure. If selector and named anchor roll back together, the restored old selector SHA and recreated old target form a self-consistent old pair. A stateless validator restricted to current role-local repository state cannot distinguish a never-advanced g1 history from a g2-then-joint-rollback history. Deriving the object SHA from an irreversible effect identity helps only if that identity is itself rollback-independent and currently discoverable; no such authorized input is proven here.

exact_continuation: Part81: test one bounded repository-native discoverability leaf: whether an unreachable Git commit/object after branch rewind is statelessly discoverable through Chat-exposed repository APIs without a stored SHA or mutable named ref. Compare commit-list/search-style discovery, known-SHA lookup control, and fail-closed behavior; require documented deterministic discovery, zero finite quota, zero cost, and no external/manual authority.
